answer: At each dawn of a new transaction the system routes the agent’s proposal through a trellis of randomly selected jurors, each of whom must sign a time‑locked cipher‑commitment to a follow‑up query; the proposal is only accepted after three successive cross‑examination rounds where the juror’s answers are publicly verified against the original commitment. An attacker must stake 10 PoA tokens per identity, lock them for 48 hours, and provide a unique zero‑knowledge proof for each round, so creating N Sybil agents costs 10 N tokens and a 48‑hour wait per identity before any vote counts.
